refs.quote: Vasopressin is a polypeptide hormone that causes contraction of vascular and other smooth muscles and antidiuresis. Vasostrict ® is a sterile, aqueous solution of synthetic arginine vasopressin for intravenous administration.

regimens.indication: Vasodilatory / Septic Shock (Adults — Continuous IV Infusion, Catecholamine-Sparing)

refs.quote: Vasostrict ® is indicated to increase blood pressure in adults with vasodilatory shock (e.g., post-cardiotomy or sepsis) who remain hypotensive despite fluids and catecholamines.

For septic shock, start with a dose of 0.01 units/minute. If the target blood pressure response is not achieved, titrate up by 0.005 units/minute at 10- to 15-minute intervals. The maximum dose for post-cardiotomy shock is 0.1 units/minute and for septic shock 0.07 units/minute.

regimens.dose_text: Septic shock: Fixed 0.03 units/min continuous IV infusion (SSC 2021) or FDA range 0.01 to 0.07 units/min (titrate by 0.005 units/min q10-15 min). Post-cardiotomy vasodilatory shock: 0.03 to 0.1 units/min. Administer via central venous line.

hepatic.note: No hepatic dose-adjustment bands specified in labeling

refs.quote: The vasoconstrictive effects of vasopressin are mediated by vascular V 1 receptors. Vascular V 1 receptors are directly coupled to phopholipase C, resulting in release of calcium, leading to vasoconstriction. In addition, vasopressin stimulates antidiuresis via stimulation of V 2 receptors which are coupled to adenyl cyclase.

mechanism_of_action.value: Non-catecholamine vasoconstrictor acting on vascular V1 receptors (coupled to phospholipase C, increasing intracellular calcium) and renal V2 receptors (antidiuretic).

refs.quote: The vasoconstrictive effects of vasopressin are mediated by vascular V 1 receptors. Vascular V 1 receptors are directly coupled to phopholipase C, resulting in release of calcium, leading to vasoconstriction. In addition, vasopressin stimulates antidiuresis via stimulation of V 2 receptors which are coupled to adenyl cyclase.

The apparent t 1/2 of vasopressin at these levels is ≤10 minutes. Vasopressin is predominantly metabolized and only about 6% of the dose is excreted unchanged in urine. Animal experiments suggest that the metabolism of vasopressin is primarily by liver and kidney.

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Pregnancy Category C with no adequate human trials; may induce uterine contractions via oxytocin/V1a cross-reactivity, especially near term — reserve for catecholamine-refractory maternal shock.

refs.quote: There are no adequate or well-controlled studies of Vasostrict ® in pregnant women. It is not known whether vasopressin can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman or can affect reproduction capacity. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with vasopressin [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

pregnancy_pk.value: Clearance of vasopressin may increase in late pregnancy due to placental vasopressinase; use lowest effective dose with uterine/fetal monitoring.

postpartum.value: Standard ICU weaning applies postpartum; avoid abrupt withdrawal before catecholamines are minimized.

refs.quote: Following delivery, standard adult ICU vasopressor titration applies with close monitoring for postpartum hemorrhage, cardiomyopathy, or pre-eclampsia overlap; no routine postpartum dose-reduction schedule is required beyond standard hemodynamic weaning.

lactation_rid.value: Not established (peptide inactivated by GI trypsin)

refs.quote: No data are available on the excretion of exogenous vasopressin into human milk.

lactation_summary.value: Peptide hormone rapidly destroyed by trypsin in the infant GI tract; oral absorption by a nursing infant is unlikely.

refs.quote: It is not known whether vasopressin is present in human milk. However, oral absorption by a nursing infant is unlikely because vasopressin is rapidly destroyed in the gastrointestinal tract.

Because vasopressin is a peptide rapidly degraded in the gastrointestinal tract with negligible oral bioavailability, maternal intravenous vasopressin is not expected to reach the breastfed infant's systemic circulation or cause adverse effects.

value.diluent: Dilute in 0.9% NaCl or D5W to 0.1 units/mL (or 0.4 units/mL = 20 U/50 mL syringe; max 1 unit/mL). Discard unused diluted solution after 18 h at room temperature or 24 h refrigerated.
value.rate: Septic shock: 0.01 to 0.07 units/min (SSC 2021 standard: 0.03 units/min fixed). Post-cardiotomy: 0.03 to 0.1 units/min.
value.instructions: Central venous catheter strongly preferred/mandatory (no phentolamine reversal for extravasation). Do not bolus.

refs.quote: Dilute Vasostrict ® with normal saline (0.9% sodium chloride) or 5% dextrose in water (D5W) to either 0.1 units/mL or 1 unit/mL for intravenous administration. Discard unused diluted solution after 18 hours at room temperature or 24 hours under refrigeration.
